result.topic_en: Derivation of the differential relations underlying Lagrange's inversion series: from x = t + uX (X a function of x) it is shown that the u-derivative of any function φx equals X times its t-derivative, leading to formulas for higher u-derivatives.
result.transcription:
$\left(\frac{dx}{dt}\right) = 1 + u\left(\frac{dX}{dt}\right) = 1 + u\left(\frac{dX}{dx}\right)\left(\frac{dx}{dt}\right)$
$\left(\frac{dx}{du}\right) = X + u\left(\frac{dX}{du}\right) = X + u\left(\frac{dX}{dx}\right)\left(\frac{dx}{du}\right)$
Hieraus $\frac{dX}{dx}$ eliminirt, gibt
$\left(\frac{dx}{du}\right) = X\left(\frac{dx}{dt}\right)$ Da nun
$\left(\frac{d\phi x}{dt}\right) = \left(\frac{d\phi x}{dx}\right)\left(\frac{dx}{dt}\right)$ und $\left(\frac{d\phi x}{du}\right) = \left(\frac{d\phi x}{dx}\right)\left(\frac{dx}{dt}\right)$ so wird [-wenn man-]
[-der Kürze wegen $\frac{d\phi x}{dx} = \phi' x$ setzt-]
$\left(\frac{d\phi x}{du}\right) = X\left(\frac{d\phi x}{dt}\right)$ ................(1)
schließlich wenn man {+statt+} $\phi x$ [-$=$-] $X$ setzt (welches erlaubt ist)
$\left(\frac{dX}{du}\right) = X\left(\frac{dX}{dt}\right)$ ................(2)
Differentiirt man auch nun (1) nach t u. u so erhält man
$\left(\frac{d^2\phi x}{dtdu}\right) = \left(\frac{dX}{dt}\right)\left(\frac{d\phi x}{dt}\right) + X\left(\frac{d^2\phi x}{dt^2}\right)$ ........(3)
$\left(\frac{d^2\phi x}{du^2}\right) = \left(\frac{dX}{du}\right)\left(\frac{d\phi x}{dt}\right) + X\left(\frac{d^2\phi x}{dtdu}\right)$
Hierin die gefundenen Werthe von $\frac{d^2\phi x}{dtdu}$ u. $\frac{dX}{du}$ substituirt gibt
$\left(\frac{d^2\phi x}{du^2}\right) =$ [-$2X\left(\frac{dX}{dt}\right)\left(\frac{d\phi x}{dt}\right) + X^2 d^2$-]
$2X\left(\frac{dX}{dt}\right)\left(\frac{d\phi x}{dt}\right) + X^2\frac{d^2\phi x}{dt^2}$ oder
$\left(\frac{d^2\phi x}{du^2}\right) = \frac{d\, X^2\frac{d\phi x}{dt}}{dt}$ .........(4)
Differentiirt man wiederum diese Gleichung nach u so wird
$\frac{d^3\phi x}{du^3} = \frac{d^2\, X^2\frac{d\phi x}{dt}}{dtdu}$. Da es aber bekanntlich gleichgültig ist ob man

methods.what: Partial derivatives of x = t + uX with respect to t and u
Chain rule giving ∂φ/∂u = X ∂φ/∂t for any function φ(x)
Mixed second derivative by differentiating (1) w.r.t. t
Second u-derivative expressed as a t-derivative: ∂²φ/∂u² = ∂/∂t (X² ∂φ/∂t)
Third u-derivative by differentiating (4) w.r.t. u, toward induction for Lagrange series
